The floodwaters are going down. For many families and communities across Southwest Colorado, the harder part is just beginning.

Over the past week, I’ve visited flood-damaged communities, talked with families and business owners, and met with local officials working to reopen roads, repair infrastructure, and help people get back home.

The immediate emergency may be passing, but recovery will take months and, in some places, years.

In my latest op-ed for the Durango Herald, I write about what I saw, what these communities need now, and why Washington needs to stay engaged for the long haul.

Read it here: https://t.co/vqqxh7pYXG #CO03

Nearly $27 million in eligible public infrastructure damage has already been identified in Archuleta and Rio Grande counties, and assessments are still underway.

That’s why @SenatorHick and I led Colorado’s bipartisan congressional delegation in urging President Trump to quickly approve Governor Polis’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration following the devastating flooding across Southwest Colorado and the San Luis Valley.

Federal disaster assistance would help communities repair damaged roads, bridges, water and wastewater systems, and other critical infrastructure, while also helping reduce the risk from future flooding.

I’ve seen the damage firsthand and talked with families, business owners, and local officials dealing with the aftermath. The need is real and recovery will take time.

This isn’t a partisan issue. We’re asking the President to approve the request quickly so these communities can get on with the work of rebuilding.

Veterans know better than anyone where the system is working and where it isn’t.

In Grand Junction yesterday, I joined veterans, state and local officials, and Colorado’s Department of Military and Veterans Affairs for a roundtable on the challenges veterans face across the Western Slope, including access to care, transportation, benefits, and support.

We finished the morning at the Veterans Memorial Cemetery of Western Colorado, where I had the chance to thank Angela Ingalls and her team for the work they do serving veterans and their families.

There is much more to do, and I’ll keep working to improve care and services for veterans across #CO03. 🇺🇸

From a rainy morning in Bayfield to a sunny afternoon in Towaoc, our Coffee with Your Congressman series continued yesterday across Southwest Colorado.

Over the past several months, we’ve held these events in Mesa, Garfield, Pueblo, La Plata, and Montezuma counties. They’re announced publicly, open to anyone from #CO03, and no RSVP is required.

The point is simple: give constituents a chance to ask me questions directly, raise concerns, offer criticism, and tell me what they’re seeing in their communities.

Thanks to everyone who joined us in Bayfield and Towaoc, and to the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe for hosting us. We’ll keep bringing these conversations across the district. Watch local news, my social media, and sign up for the Hurd Huddle for upcoming events.

Thank you to everyone from La Plata and Archuleta Counties who joined me in Bayfield this morning for Coffee with Your Congressman!

We had a good conversation about the issues facing our communities, and I appreciated the thoughtful questions, honest feedback, and even some constructive criticism. You don’t have to agree with me to have a seat at the table. Listening to the people I represent is one of the most important parts of my job.

Next stop: Towaoc!

Water is inseparable from the future of the Lower Arkansas Valley.

I stopped by the Lower Arkansas Valley Water Conservancy District today in Rocky Ford to hear directly from the people working to protect the Valley’s water, agriculture, and rural communities.

After a difficult water year, and with important questions ahead about agricultural water, revegetation, and municipal water purchases, the federal government needs to know where it can be useful. 

Thank you to Board Chairman Leroy Mauch and the board, as well as General Manager Jack Goble, for the thoughtful conversation. #CO03

Pueblo has jobs to fill. The challenge is making sure people have the training to fill them.

A new $10.7 million Department of Labor grant puts Pueblo Community College at the center of a statewide effort to close that gap. PCC will lead a 15-institution consortium building a system that helps students earn portable credentials tied to skills employers actually need. 

That matters in Pueblo, where employers, including manufacturers, need skilled workers, and it gives students a clearer path from the classroom to a good job. 

It’s a significant role for PCC and a good example of what community colleges can do for the economies they serve.

Read more in the Pueblo Chieftain: https://t.co/WbYhbIiQGE

I welcomed DOE Office of Indian Energy Director Eric Mahroum to Grand Junction to discuss Tribal energy development and how we can better support Tribal sovereignty.

The Southern Ute Indian Tribe is leading the way as the first Tribe in the nation to enter into a Tribal Energy Resource Agreement, giving it greater control over energy development on its own lands.

Tribal Nations know their resources best. Washington should be focused on removing barriers, not standing in their way. #CO03

Some of the best opportunities for students in Western Colorado are right here at home.

I recently toured Colorado Mesa University’s Montrose campus with Director Steve Metheny to see how they’re preparing students for good-paying careers in nursing, welding, machining, and law enforcement.

The campus serves roughly 500 students, and its practical nursing program has been ranked #1 in the nation for two consecutive years. That’s an impressive accomplishment and a testament to the students, faculty, and staff.

In rural Colorado, students should be able to learn valuable skills, find good-paying jobs, and build a future right here at home. Programs like these make that possible while strengthening our local workforce.

Thank you to Steve and the entire CMU Montrose team for the important work you’re doing for Western Colorado. #CO03

I disagree with the Administration’s decision to waive new sanctions Congress passed to increase economic pressure on Russia.

Putin started this war, and Russia continues its brutal attacks on Ukrainian civilians and critical infrastructure. I understand the need to lower energy costs for American families. But easing sanctions makes it easier for Russia to fund its war, with little evidence that Americans will see meaningful savings.

I support efforts to bring this war to an end. But a lasting peace requires accountability, and we should not ease pressure on Russia without meaningful concessions in return.

I hope the Administration reconsiders.

I appreciate my colleagues on both sides of the aisle for helping pass my bipartisan Geothermal Energy Advancement Act through the House.

Good news for communities in Pueblo County still recovering from the Aspen Acres Fire and flooding: the SBA has approved low-interest disaster loans for eligible homeowners, renters, businesses, and nonprofits.

For a family, that can mean help repairing a damaged home or replacing a car, furniture, or other belongings. For a small business, it can mean help repairing property or covering payroll and bills while recovery continues. 

These are loans, not grants, but for people facing uninsured losses they can be an important part of rebuilding.

Beginning Monday, October 19, SBA staff will be available in Pueblo to answer questions and help people apply. Walk-ins are welcome. 

This is one more piece of the recovery effort, and I’ll keep working for the additional help these communities need.

A lot of the issues that matter most to Western and Southern Colorado—water, public lands, forests, energy, and wildlife—come through the House Natural Resources Committee.

Since taking office, I’ve tried to use my seat on the committee to turn Colorado priorities into legislation. This graphic shows the progress so far on my Natural Resources bills. We’ve moved bills dealing with Crystal Reservoir and Western water, advanced major geothermal permitting reforms, and gotten bipartisan conservation legislation signed into law.

There’s plenty left to do, and I’ll keep working across the aisle where we can get results for #CO03.

A good job provides more than a paycheck. It offers purpose, dignity, independence, and the opportunity to contribute to your community.

In Pueblo, Pueblo Diversified Industries (PDI) is doing important work helping people with disabilities develop job skills, find meaningful employment, and build more independent lives.

This week, PDI and SourceAmerica presented me with the AbilityOne Congressional Champion Award for my work supporting employment opportunities for people with disabilities.

I appreciate the recognition, but the real credit belongs to the dedicated team at PDI and the individuals whose hard work and determination make these programs successful.

Everyone deserves the opportunity to work, contribute, and build a better future. I’m grateful for the work PDI is doing to make that possible in Pueblo and across Southern Colorado.

I was proud to work with President Hazelbaker and the Department of Labor to help secure $10.7 million for Pueblo Community College to expand workforce training and connect more students with good-paying jobs.

Investing in our local workforce means creating opportunities for young people to build their careers and raise their families right here in Southern Colorado.

Thank you to President Hazelbaker and @Sonderling47 for their partnership and commitment to Pueblo. #CO03

Social media usually gives me only a minute or two to cover something. My Hurd in the House podcast gives me a chance to slow down and actually have a conversation.

Here are a few behind-the-scenes shots from recording my latest episode at Pueblo Community College with Army veteran Jacobo Varela. We talked about his experience with the VA, where the system works, where it doesn’t, and what veterans want Washington to understand. #CO03

You can watch this episode (and catch up on earlier episodes of Hurd in the House) here: https://t.co/mRYMm9lTTZ

For 251 years, the United States Navy has defended our country and protected American interests at sea and around the world.

Today, we thank the sailors serving now, the veterans who served before them, and their families.

Happy Birthday, U.S. Navy. 🇺🇸⚓ #CO03 https://t.co/uAK3phyXC9

Veterans across Southern Colorado deserve timely access to the care and benefits they’ve earned through their service.

Last week, I welcomed VA Secretary Doug Collins to Pueblo Community College to hear directly from local veterans about the challenges they face, particularly in rural communities.

We discussed improving access to care, expanding mental health services, and making the VA more responsive to the veterans it serves.

Pueblo is the Home of Heroes, and we have a responsibility to stand by the men and women who have served our country. I appreciate Secretary Collins coming to Southern Colorado, listening to our veterans, and working with us to address these challenges.

I’ll keep fighting to make sure veterans across Western and Southern Colorado get the care and benefits they’ve earned.

Read more from FOX21 News ⬇️

https://t.co/QHuC0EU2Kc

Hurd in the House Episode 13 is live on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and YouTube!

This week, I sat down with Jacobo Varela, Executive Director of TRIO College Opportunity Programs and Director of Veterans Upward Bound at Colorado State University Pueblo. A U.S. Army veteran, Jacobo has spent more than a decade helping veterans in Southern Colorado find resources and new opportunities.

We talked about the challenges veterans can face when navigating benefits and services, where to turn for help, and how education and community connections can support the transition to civilian life. Take a listen! #CO03

Spotify: https://t.co/2fjnaLplzv 

YouTube: https://t.co/mRYMm9lm4r

When a wildfire starts, every minute matters.

At a hearing on disaster prevention, I asked John Gale of Pano AI how faster detection can help firefighters respond sooner.

In Douglas County, Pano’s system alerted response agencies within minutes of detecting the Bear Creek Fire. A local helitack crew responded, and the fire was contained to less than three acres.

Technology like this can give firefighters something they rarely have enough of: time. #CO03 

Watch the rest of my questioning here: https://t.co/SGV8B5QmR2

I have raised concerns directly with the White House and Pentagon about reports that the Administration may livestream Nidal Hasan’s execution.

Hasan murdered 13 people and wounded 32 others at Fort Hood. His crimes were horrific, and he deserves to face justice. But how our government administers justice matters. We should not broadcast an execution to the world.

I hope the Administration reconsiders.

https://t.co/rK8TCzbTjP

Great turnout at the Pueblo Police Department’s open house!

Thank you to Chief Chris Noeller and the entire @PuebloPolice1 team for the opportunity to see their work firsthand, tour the real-time crime center, and get a better understanding of the training officers go through.

Our law enforcement officers put themselves on the line every day to keep our communities safe. I’m grateful for their service and will always stand with the men and women who protect Pueblo.

#ILovePueblo #CO03

The devastating wildfires and flooding across Southern Colorado have destroyed homes, displaced families, and left communities facing a long road to recovery.

Last month, I brought Western Caucus Chair @RepMaloyUtah and Chairmen @RepWesterman and @RepBrianBabin to Southern Colorado to see firsthand the damage from the Aspen Acres and Gold Mountain Fires and the challenges our communities continue to face.

I appreciate my colleagues taking the time to see what families in our district are up against. Recovering and rebuilding won’t happen overnight, and I’ll keep working to make sure our communities have the federal support they need to get back on their feet. #CO03

Read more from CBS Colorado: https://t.co/jpNQL1xJMZ

Thank you to Secretary Collins for coming to Pueblo, the Home of Heroes, to hear directly from our veterans and local leaders.

We’ve made progress reducing VA processing times, but there’s more work to do. Veterans across Western and Southern Colorado deserve timely, reliable care and the benefits they’ve earned through their service.

I’ll keep fighting to make sure they get both. #CO03

Protecting Western Colorado’s water shouldn’t be partisan.

At the Colorado River District’s Annual Water Seminar 2026, @SenatorBennet and I talked about how we worked across two administrations to secure and release $40 million for the Shoshone water right, and why that same kind of cooperation will matter as we deal with the future of the Colorado River. 

My bottom line on what comes next: any Upper Basin conservation needs to be fair, voluntary, compensated, and temporary. And it cannot come on the backs of our farmers and ranchers. #CO03

If you’d like to watch our full conversation at the 2026 Annual Water Seminar, click this link: https://t.co/IvaNvwZDpL

Three years ago, Hamas terrorists carried out the deadliest attack against the Jewish people since the Holocaust, murdering more than 1,200 people and taking more than 250 hostage.

I will never forget visiting Kibbutz Nir Oz and seeing firsthand what was left behind after the October 7 attacks.

Today, we remember the innocent lives taken that day, stand with Jewish communities against antisemitism and hatred, and reaffirm our support for Israel’s security and its right to exist.

We will not forget October 7.

posts.text:
Reminder to student entrepreneurs across #CO03: there’s still time to apply for America250’s America’s Startup competition.

Undergraduate college and trade school students with an early-stage business idea can apply individually or in teams of up to five. Thirty semifinalist teams will be invited to Washington, D.C., to pitch in person, and finalists can receive up to $50,000 to help develop their businesses.

Western and Southern Colorado are full of young people with good ideas. If you’ve been thinking about starting something, this is worth a look.

Applications are due October 8. Learn more and apply through: https://t.co/JhOjRh7VBA

Western Colorado has skilled manufacturers doing work that contributes directly to our national defense.

I toured Valor Tactical with CEO Jan Zickerman and learned more about the company’s engineering and manufacturing work here in Mesa County, including mounts for a .50-caliber M2 machine gun that Valor is currently putting through live-fire testing.

Valor is a good example of how Western Colorado’s manufacturing expertise can support our servicemembers while creating skilled jobs here at home. #CO03

Geothermal can produce reliable American energy around the clock. We should be doing a lot more with it.

That’s why I’m co-chairing the new bipartisan Congressional Geothermal Caucus with @RepSalinas, @RepAuchincloss, and @RepNickBegich.

Republicans and Democrats agree there’s an opportunity here. Our job now is to find practical ways to get more geothermal projects built, strengthen the grid, and meet America’s growing demand for energy. 

Colorado has real potential to be part of that future. #CO03

Read more: https://t.co/K1QYCfYuDD

Colorado’s Third District is full of talented students with the creativity and skills to build what comes next.

The Congressional App Challenge gives middle and high school students across #CO03 a chance to turn an idea into an app and put their coding and problem-solving skills to work.

Submissions are due October 26. Learn more about eligibility and how to enter at https://t.co/1biDXbFMDq.

I’m looking forward to seeing what students across Western and Southern Colorado create.

Barbora and I were saddened to learn of Justice Melissa Hart’s passing. I had great respect for her work as a jurist and public servant, and Barbora had the opportunity to know her through her work with Colorado’s judicial review commission.

Melissa was a remarkable intellect, a dedicated teacher, and a committed public servant. Colorado is better for her years of service.

Our thoughts and prayers are with Kevin, their children, and everyone who knew and loved her. May she rest in peace.

https://t.co/1CuWtYlA6G

Saturday night at @ColoradoMesaU was all about rodeo, Western heritage, and the next generation carrying both forward.

Thank you to CMU’s rodeo coaches and everyone who supports these student-athletes, and to keynote speaker Leon Vick for sharing his experience and commitment to https://t.co/B0u16eC36f

Broncos have a bye week, so we took matters into our own hands. One of us literally. 

My four year-old drew up the play himself. Nobody else understood it, but he seemed confident. 

Go Broncos. #CO03 https://t.co/7JL2P200J4

Local newspapers play an important role in our communities. They keep us informed, hold us accountable, and give neighbors a place to exchange ideas, even when they disagree.

This week, I recognized Ellen Stein on the House floor for her years of service to Southwest Colorado as https://t.co/8A60vKNNEO

Western Colorado’s energy industry has supported generations of families and remains an important part of our economy. Its future depends on investing in the next generation.

I joined West Slope COGA at Colorado Mesa University for its annual Sips and Scholarships event to recognize students preparing for careers in energy and the people helping them succeed.

I also presented Quint Shear with a Congressional Record tribute recognizing his decades of leadership and service to Western Colorado. Congratulations to Quint on receiving the 2026 Fred Julander Lifetime Achievement Award.

Thank you to West Slope COGA for supporting our students and strengthening the future of Western Colorado’s energy industry. #CO03

The floodwaters are going down. For many families and communities across Southwest Colorado, the harder part is just beginning.

Over the past week, I’ve visited flood-damaged communities, talked with families and business owners, and met with local officials working to reopen roads, repair infrastructure, and help people get back home.

The immediate emergency may be passing, but recovery will take months and, in some places, years.

In my latest op-ed for the Durango Herald, I write about what I saw, what these communities need now, and why Washington needs to stay engaged for the long haul.

Read it here: https://t.co/vqqxh7pYXG #CO03
